original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: For the explicit abstract F2[Q8] alphabet D_N(g)=I+(g+1)N with 28 binary rank-one idempotents and g in Q8 minus the identity, exclude one- and two-factor realizations of diag(i,j,k), and verify a three-factor realization.
scope_change_reason: The general new-register card is narrowed to a fixed nonabelian Q8 label algebra, a specified three-register target and the complete one- and two-factor boundary. This isolates whether noncommuting group labels can save one paid factor in a finite, exact alphabet.
bottleneck_link: The target is a three-register bit primitive in a changed label algebra. Each abstract factor is charged one unit; a two-factor realization would be a strict one-unit saving over the direct three-factor control. No physical supplier or recursive interface is established.
stop_rule: Exhaust exactly 28*7 one-factor words and 28*7*28*7 ordered two-factor words, verify the three-factor positive control and independent replay, then stop. Do not extend to longer words in this cycle.
evidence: The one-factor census has 196 words, zero hits and minimum coefficient Hamming distance 4. The two-factor census has 38,416 words, zero hits and minimum distance 2 (six words). A direct three-factor word equals diag(i,j,k). A set-based verifier independently recomputes both censuses, checks all 64 Q8 products and all 512 associativity triples, verifies the 28 idempotents and rejects a non-idempotent control. This is an exact finite exclusion only for the stated alphabet.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance: model formalization, Python implementation, independent set-based verifier, exact replay and package documentation. The scope claim was posted by the author in Discussion #2300.

open_questions.question: Can a physical supplier implement one Q8-labeled factor with a complete all-size interface at less than one rank-one factor's cost after conversion and restoration?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A favorable supplier could make this nonabelian label model relevant to the conditional integer-multiplication bound; the current algebraic census alone cannot affect that bound.
open_questions.first_step: Map one D_N(g) to a concrete source and interface schedule, then charge source access, child calls, conversions, hosting, restoration and precision.
open_questions.blocked_by: No physical supplier or all-size implementation for D_N(g) is identified in this contribution.
